newsitem.title: CROATIA: Drugs firm Pliva steals show on Croatian bourse.
newsitem.headline: Drugs firm Pliva steals show on Croatian bourse.

text.p: Croatian drugs firm Pliva stole the show amid bouyant market activity on Zagreb Stock Exchange on Tuesday, selling over 10,000 shares, traders said.
"Pliva has recorded over 70 transactions, and demand for it is still high," a trader of CAIB said.
It opened at 480 kuna, down four from last Thursday when it last traded but later peaked at 510 kuna. Traders said Pliva's bid and ask prices in Zagreb were now hovering between 502 and 506 kuna.
Its Global Depository Receipts (GDRs) trading in London were also on the rise, fetching $16.325 by 1000GMT, after opening at $16.1.
The firm sold an average of 300 shares per package by noon in Zagreb, although several transactions amounted to over 1,000 shares sold.
Pliva last week fluctuated below 500 kuna in what traders described as a correction after its previous climb.
Closing prices on the Zagreb Stock Exchange are available on page ZAGSTOCK each afternoon from Tuesday to Friday.
